statement: A drawer holds $8$ red socks, $8$ blue socks, $8$ green socks and $8$ white socks. In the dark, Leo pulls out socks one at a time. What is the smallest number of socks he must pull out to be sure he has two matching pairs? A matching pair is two socks of the same color, and the two pairs may be the same color, so four red socks count as two pairs.

choices.misconception: I found how many socks guarantee one matching pair, 4 + 1 = 5, and stopped there.
I thought one sock of each color plus 2 more socks would give two pairs, so I said 4 + 2 = 6.
I thought each pair needs its own worst case of 5 socks, so I doubled 5 to get 10.
I solved a different problem, getting four socks of one color, with 3 socks of each color plus 1, which is 13.

hints: Find the largest handful of socks that still does not contain two pairs.
With only one pair, you can have at most 3 socks of one color (4 socks of one color already make two pairs) and at most 1 sock of each other color.
That worst handful is 3 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 6 socks. One more sock forces a second pair.

solutions.reliable: Six socks are not enough: $3$ red, $1$ blue, $1$ green and $1$ white contain only one pair. Now take any $7$ socks and suppose they held at most one pair. Then at most one color could have $2$ or more socks, and that color would have at most $3$ socks, since $4$ socks of one color make two pairs. Each other color would have at most $1$ sock, for a total of at most $3 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 6$ socks, which is impossible. So $7$ socks always contain two matching pairs, and the answer is $7$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
